data.claim: The three recovery detectors are judgment over plain facts, not new I/O: a non-live lease whose holder's process is provably alive is lapsed_alive (never crashed); an unfinished item with commits ahead and only 'merge' owed is ready_to_land (never landed); a worktree mid-merge or a branch head strict-behind the base with no logged merge is merge_interrupted
data.falsifier: a lease lapsed while its holder lives reports kind 'lapsed_alive' with pids, and NEVER 'crashed'
data.mechanism: extend core.health with LAPSED_ALIVE/READY_TO_LAND/MERGE_INTERRUPTED finding kinds over new Lane.lapsed_alive + Ready + MergeHang facts, and the boot id compared in infra/worktree._boot over /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id stored in .ddflow/local/boot

chunk_findings.detail: `stored_boot` promises to return `""` when no boot id was recorded and `observe_boot` promises that reading never raises, but it catches only `OSError`. If `.ddflow/local/boot` exists and contains invalid UTF-8 bytes, e.g. `b"\xff"`, then `Path.read_text("utf-8")` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is not caught. In that state `observe_boot(repo)` propagates the exception and crashes the health pass instead of returning a result with `changed=False`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_boot.py:34-39

chunk_findings.detail: `observe_boot` conflates an unreadable previous marker with a missing one. If the marker file already contains the current boot id but is read-denied while still writable, e.g. file mode `0222`, then `stored_boot` catches `PermissionError` and returns `""`; with a readable current boot id this makes `cur != prev`, so `observe_boot` writes the marker and returns `changed=True` even though no reboot occurred. That can license a post-reboot recovery sweep from an unchanged/unknown previous state, violating the module’s stated “unknown is not no” / never-run-an-unlicensed-sweep requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_boot.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The new recovery kinds are resolved through the same generic mode loop as correction kinds, so a global mode override can make them `apply`. For example, with `override="apply"` (e.g. `ddflow health --mode apply`) or `[health].mode=apply`, `own.get(k, "inherit")` returns `"inherit"` for `LAPSED_ALIVE`, `READY_TO_LAND`, and `MERGE_INTERRUPTED`, and the loop returns `"apply"` for those keys. The added comment states these detectors have no apply correction and “never apply anything”; returning `apply` for them routes the health engine down an apply path for a detector that has no correction (or records it as applied) without `recover` performing the recovery.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_modes

chunk_findings.detail: The `landed_unlogged` detector uses “branch head is an ancestor of `base`, and `base` has commits beyond the branch” as proof that a merge landed without being logged. That shape is also exactly what an empty or stale branch has. For example, an item has `branch = "feature/x"` created from `main` at commit `A`, but no commits have been added to `feature/x`; `main` then advances to commit `B`. `_merges` runs `rev-parse refs/heads/feature/x` and gets `A`, `merge-base --is-ancestor A main` succeeds, and `rev-list --count refs/heads/feature/x..main` returns `1`, so it appends `MergeHang(... landed_unlogged=True)`. This is wrong: `rev-list --count main..feature/x` is `0`, no work landed, and the branch is merely an empty/stale branch created from a commit already contained in `main`. The code never checks the empty-branch condition its comment says it excludes, so ordinary branches created from an older base, reset to base, or otherwise having no unique commits can be misreported as landed-unlogged merge hangs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_merges

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that a lane owing more than `merge` is not proposed to land, but it never calls `H.inspect` and only asserts that the constructed `Ready` object's `owed` attribute is truthy. For the input `H.Ready("T1", "a", commits_ahead=1, owed=("unit_tests", "merge"))`, the assertion passes even if `H.inspect` returns a `ready_to_land` finding for that item, so the test cannot catch a regression that incorrectly proposes landing when work remains beyond merge.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recovery_detectors.py:TestReadyToLand.test_more_than_merge_owed_is_not_ready_to_land

chunk_findings.detail: When the marker is present but unreadable, the `except (OSError, UnicodeError)` branch returns `changed=False` immediately and never writes the current boot id. Given `.ddflow/local/boot` containing invalid UTF-8 bytes (e.g. `b"\xff"`), the first `observe_boot(repo)` leaves the marker corrupt. If the machine later reboots and `boot_id()` changes, the next call still reads the same invalid marker, catches `UnicodeError`, and again returns `changed=False`; the detector is permanently stuck and never licenses the intended post-reboot recovery. The docstring says `observe_boot` records the current boot id and that unknown is not no; when the previous value is unknown but writing is possible, it should still update the marker with `changed=False`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_boot.py:observe_boot

chunk_findings.detail: The new `landed_unlogged` check only requires the branch tip to be a strict descendant of `it.base_sha` and an ancestor of `base`. That still accepts an empty branch that was fast-forwarded/reset to the current base. For example, with `it.base_sha = A`, `it.branch = feature/x`, and `base = main` advanced linearly from `A` to `B`, if `feature/x` has no commits of its own but was simply synced to `main` so `refs/heads/feature/x == B`, then `fork != head` is true, `merge-base --is-ancestor A B` succeeds, and `merge-base --is-ancestor B B` succeeds. `_merges` therefore appends a `MergeHang(... landed_unlogged=True, head=B, base=B)` finding even though no branch work landed unlogged; the branch tip is just the base. The fix excludes the empty tip-equals-fork case, but not the empty synced-to-base case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_merges

chunk_findings.detail: `_readies` only filters out owed gates that are not `"merge"`; it never requires `commits_ahead > 0`. Given a `Ready` row for a branch that is empty or already contained in its base, e.g. `Ready("T1", "a", commits_ahead=0, owed=("merge",), branch="feature/x")`, the function returns a `READY_TO_LAND` finding whose detail is `"0 commit(s) ahead ..."` and whose fix proposes `ddflow merge T1`. If the branch has no commits ahead of the base, there is nothing to land, so this detector emits a false recovery signal rather than no finding (or a landed/unlogged-style finding).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/health.py:_readies

chunk_findings.detail: The landed-unlogged branch is selected before considering `m.merging`. If a `MergeHang` is constructed with both `merging=True` and `landed_unlogged=True`—which the bool fields permit—`_merge_hangs` returns the landed-unlogged detail/fix (`"record merge and complete ..."`) and ignores that a merge is still mid-flight. For example, `MergeHang(item="T1", holder="a", merging=True, landed_unlogged=True, tree="wt", head="abc...", base="main")` produces a finding advising to record the merge while `MERGE_HEAD`/mid-merge state is still present, which is unsafe; the mid-flight case should take precedence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/health.py:_merge_hangs

chunk_findings.detail: `observe_boot` replaces `.ddflow/local/boot` with `Path.write_text`, which truncates the file before writing. If that replacement is interrupted after truncation (for example, the process is killed, or a transient disk-full/EIO write fails and space is later freed), the marker can be left empty. On the next call, `prev` is read as `""`, `cur` is the unchanged boot id, and the code treats that empty marker as a first sighting: `cur != prev`, it writes the marker, and returns `changed=True`. This fabricates a reboot from a corrupt/unknown previous marker and can license a post-reboot recovery sweep even though no reboot occurred, contrary to the module’s stated invariant that unknown is not no and that the detector must not report a reboot from an unreadable/unknown marker.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_boot.py:65

chunk_findings.detail: `_merges` reports any item worktree with `W.merging(wt) is True` as a `MergeHang`, without checking whether the item’s lease is still live or how long the merge has been in progress; the function does not even receive `now`. For a non-removed, non-terminal item whose lease is live (an agent is actively resolving a merge conflict) and whose worktree contains `MERGE_HEAD`, `_merges` returns a finding. Because recovery detector kinds can be acted on by `recover` under SAFE_AUTO, this can classify an active merge as an interrupted/hung merge and license recovery while the merge is still being worked on.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:_merges

chunk_findings.detail: The new precedence test does not actually verify that a mid-flight merge takes precedence over a landed-unlogged tag. If `_merge_hangs` regressed to the old behavior and returned the landed-unlogged advice for a `MergeHang` with both `merging=True` and `landed_unlogged=True`, this test could still pass: `evidence["merging"]` would still be `True` because the input field is `True`, and a landed-unlogged fix such as “record merge and complete …” would satisfy `"re-merge" not in f.fix.lower() or "abort" in f.fix`. The test therefore gives false confidence that the known “record merge while MERGE_HEAD is set” defect is fixed, while it never asserts that the fix/detail omits landed-unlogged guidance.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recovery_detectors.py:test_merging_takes_precedence_over_landed_unlogged

chunk_findings.detail: The zero-commits test is vacuous for the claimed guard because it constructs `H.Ready("T1", "a", 0, ())` with no owed merge gate. If `_readies` only emits `READY_TO_LAND` when a `"merge"` owed gate is present, this input produces no finding regardless of `commits_ahead`. A regression that still emits `READY_TO_LAND` for `commits_ahead=0` when `owed=("merge",)` would pass this test unchanged. The test should use the owed gate that actually triggers `READY_TO_LAND` to demonstrate that zero commits ahead is ignored.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recovery_detectors.py:test_zero_commits_ahead_is_not_ready_to_land
